notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on the building's date: NRHP record and LOC essay say fog signal building/horn 1909; LighthouseFriends says south pier works 1912, tower atop fog signal building 1931. The NRHP nomination PDF on npgallery is an image placeholder and was not readable, so only the Wisconsin Historical Society's summary record was used. The NR record says the existing optic is a Fresnel lens; LighthouseFriends says it was removed June 2019. The LHB 1892 evidence quote is the move date of the front range light from the fiscal 1892 report in the 1891-1892 volume; the 1891 range-light facts about the rear tower rest on LighthouseFriends alone. The 1896-97 volume covers two reports, so the Ulida walk damage is not pinned to one year. The 1900 report's 608 hours was matched in the OCR text near 'Kewaunee jjierhead (rear)'; it is the fog signal serving the rear/pierhead station, check by page image. LighthouseFriends quotes the 1888 Light-House Board report and the 1837 Pendergrast report second-hand; the story cites it as such. Newspaper search found nothing for Petersen's 1901 loss on Chronicling America; the Kewaunee Enterprise (Friends site /newspapers page) was not read. Story states Ryan 'principal keeper' 1970-71 from the USLHS roster only. The 2022 NRHP listing year comes from our station record; the Society's press-release page read does not print a date (its wispolitics copy returned 403), so the story gives no year. Fact-check 2026-10-27: removed unsourced 'third arrangement', 'white', 'covered' and 'worst event'; stated the 1909 (LOC) vs 1919 (LighthouseFriends) diaphone disagreement. The 608-hours/44-tons figure is in the fiscal 1900 report (listed 'Kewaunee pierhead (rear)', whistles in duplicate); a different 608-hours/57-tons entry appears in the 1896-97 volume.
